meta.name: SWARM
meta.note: Single source of truth for every number shown on the site. Values come from the published SWARM mainnet launch manifest (rendered 2026-09-26T12:23:33Z). Edit here, then mirror the same values in the static HTML fallbacks (see README.md).

status.ribbon: SWARM mainnet is live · run a node, mine a block, send a shielded payment.
status.detail: SWARM mainnet went live on 26 September 2026 at 12:25 UTC. There was no sale, no presale and no token offering; every SWM is mined.

chain.lineage: Proven open-source code with consensus rules and cryptography left unmodified.

genesis.note: Read from the published mainnet launch manifest (network/swarm-mainnet/manifest.json, sha256 c5ee6cf83985a529a46d32366eae82d939c23c2b38ffb85541b74c1e96f76d25). The baseline-miner payout address is operational, not consensus, and is deliberately not listed.
genesis.custody: Each script is controlled by three key shares generated offline at the launch key ceremony and held under the custody policy published with the launch manifest; two of the three are needed to spend.

rewardSplit.label: Fixed in the genesis rules for the whole emission schedule. Paid block by block as part of each block reward — not a premine.
rewardSplit.appliesFor: The whole emission schedule. Every halving reduces all four amounts proportionally, keeping the same 80 / 8 / 4 / 8 structure, until block rewards reach zero.
rewardSplit.destinations: Each allocation is paid automatically to its predefined destination address. Destinations can only be changed through a formal protocol upgrade; the percentages themselves cannot be changed.

shares.name: Miner
shares.desc: Paid to the forager who found the block.

shares.name: Core Development
shares.desc: Funds work on the node, indexer and wallet.

shares.name: Grants & Ecosystem
shares.desc: Funds tooling, documentation and community work.

shares.name: Community & Development Reserve
shares.desc: Set aside for the community and for future development. How it is governed and spent will be defined separately and published before mainnet launches.

lifetimeTotals.note: Amounts are exact to the smallest unit for the first seven eras (about 28 years). After that the inherited rounding rule rounds each allocation down to a whole unit and the miner receives the remainder, which is why the lifetime miner share is fractionally above 80%.

emission.note: Cumulative supply over the first 20 years, derived from block time, block reward and halving interval.

apps.name: SWARM Wallet
apps.detail: Hold, send and receive — transparent or shielded. Windows, Linux, macOS and Android.

apps.name: SWARM Node
apps.detail: One app runs a full node and lets you start or stop CPU mining with one click. Consent-first — nothing runs hidden.

apps.name: SWARM Explorer
apps.detail: Every block, every transaction, every allocation.

roadmap.name: SWARM mainnet
roadmap.detail: The coin, the chain, SWARM Node with one-click mining, SWARM Wallet on desktop and Android, the block explorer.

roadmap.name: Growing the swarm
roadmap.detail: More nodes and miners; the wallet in the App Store and on Google Play; signed builds on every platform.

roadmap.name: SWARM Market
roadmap.detail: An online marketplace where merchants list and buyers pay in SWM, shielded by default, without custody.

roadmap.name: Privacy browser
roadmap.detail: A browser with the SWARM wallet built in: one-click payments, private by default, nothing phoning home.

roadmap.name: Private messaging
roadmap.detail: End-to-end encrypted messages between wallets with payments inside the conversation; keys kept apart from spending keys.

endpoints.note: The public addresses of the live mainnet. seed-main is a peer address, not a web address: never open it as https://.
endpoints.rpcNote: Loopback only. The node RPC is never exposed publicly.

addressFormats.note: What a SWARM address looks like, so you can tell at a glance which network you are on.

formats.detail: Unified shielded address. The default in SWARM Wallet.
Pay-to-script-hash, used by the three fund addresses and by mining payouts.
The public testnet keeps its own prefix. Testnet coins have no value.

deliveries.note: What has actually shipped, what is being built now, and what is only planned. Rendered on /roadmap. Rules: 'live' means the public can use it today and the date is the day it became public; 'in-development' means work has started and there is no date; 'planned' means it has not started and gets neither a date nor a promise.

items.name: Public testnet
items.detail: The first public SWARM chain, mined in the open. It is still running, still published, and its coins have no value.

items.name: SWARM mainnet
items.detail: Block 1 mined in public at 12:25 UTC from a genesis block holding nothing. No sale, no presale, no premine.

items.name: Mainnet block explorer
items.detail: mainnet.explore.swarm.green, showing SwarmMainnet. The testnet explorer keeps running alongside it.

items.name: SWARM Node for Windows, Linux and macOS
items.detail: A full node and a one-click CPU miner in one app: installer and portable zip for Windows, .deb and AppImage for Linux, signed and notarized disk image and zip for macOS, each with its SHA-256.

items.name: SWARM Wallet for Windows, Linux and macOS
items.detail: Hold, send and receive SWM, shielded or transparent. It checks the chain label and the genesis before it syncs or sends anything. The macOS packages are unsigned.

items.name: Wallet SDK, swarm-sdk-mainnet-1
items.detail: The light-wallet SDK carrying the SWARM mainnet network definition, published so other wallets can be built against the same chain.

items.name: Signed SWARM Wallet for macOS
items.detail: SWARM Node for Apple silicon and Intel is signed and notarized. The mainnet Mac wallet remains unsigned; its signed build is being prepared on the owner’s Mac.

items.name: Mobile wallets in the app stores
items.detail: The Android mainnet wallet is published as a direct APK you install yourself. The Google Play listing and the iPhone build are being prepared.

items.name: SWARM Market
items.detail: A marketplace where merchants list what they sell and buyers pay in SWM, shielded by default and without custody. Non-custodial invoices come first; escrow, multisignature and dispute handling need their own protocol and operational review before any of it ships.

items.name: A wider operator network
items.detail: More full nodes in more places, starting with machines the project runs itself and opening out from there. The Swarm map shows the cities whose operators asked to be listed.

items.name: A second seed node
items.detail: One seed node is one failure domain. A second seed in a different network and a different provider removes the single point that new nodes currently bootstrap from.

items.name: Custody tooling for the three funds
items.detail: The 2-of-3 signing procedure for the published fund addresses has been exercised end to end. The tooling and the written policy around it are being finished so the process is repeatable and reviewable, not improvised.

items.name: An independent security review
items.detail: A review of the code as it was launched, by people who did not write it. Its findings will be published, including the ones that are uncomfortable.

items.name: A pool protocol for miners
items.detail: Today every miner is solo. A pool needs a work-distribution protocol, share accounting and an answer to who holds rewards before they are paid out — that last part needs review before it exists.

items.name: Exchange and SDK integrations
items.detail: Making SWM reachable from software the project does not write. Nothing is agreed, nothing is announced, and no listing is promised.

items.name: Privacy browser
items.detail: A browser with the SWARM wallet built in: pay from the address bar, trackers blocked, nothing phoning home, and each site given only the permissions you grant it.

items.name: Private messaging
items.detail: End-to-end encrypted messages between wallets, with payments inside the conversation and chat identities kept apart from spending keys.
